content.title: About
content.content: Espresso is a concentrated coffee beverage made by forcing hot water under high pressure through finely ground coffee. It features a strong aroma, a thick crema on top, and a characteristic bittersweet flavor. Espresso serves as the base for many coffee drinks such as latte, cappuccino, and Americano.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “espresso” comes from Italian meaning “fast”, because the drink is prepared in 25‑30 seconds.
The first commercial espresso machine was invented in 1901 in Italy by Luigi Bezzera.
Crema is an emulsion of oils and gases that forms only under proper pressure (about 9 bar).
Espresso accounts for more than 70 % of all coffee beans consumed worldwide.
In Japan, “siphon espresso” is popular, where water passes through coffee under vacuum rather than pressure.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Espresso contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cognitive function
items.content: Caffeine improves attention, reaction time, and short‑term memory, especially with moderate intake.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Caffeine increases thermogenesis, leading to a modest rise in calorie expenditure.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Espresso supplies magnesium, potassium, and manganese, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Enhances mood
items.content: Caffeine raises dopamine and serotonin levels, which can improve mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive consumption.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Espresso can aggravate gastritis and reflux symptoms in susceptible people.

items.title: Impact on bone health
items.content: High caffeine intake may increase calcium excretion, so those at risk of osteoporosis should limit consumption.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and diminish the efficacy of sedative medications.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Espresso is served in small cups (30‑40 ml) immediately after extraction to preserve the crema. It can be enjoyed straight or used as a base for latte, cappuccino, macchiato, and Americano. Optional additions include a pinch of sugar, milk, or flavored syrups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dark place, preferably refrigerated, but use within a month. For optimal flavor, store whole beans and grind them just before pulling an espresso shot.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato tots are small bite‑size pieces of grated potato that are coated in a seasoned breadcrumb crust, flash‑frozen and intended for oven baking. When baked they develop a crisp golden exterior while remaining soft and fluffy inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tots are a classic side dish for burgers and salads in North America.
Freezing locks in flavor and texture, allowing quick preparation any time.
In the United States and Canada they are commonly called "tater tots".
A high‑starch potato variety is used to achieve the characteristic bite.
Baking instead of deep‑frying reduces added fat compared with traditional fries.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: A modest amount of vitamin C remains after freezing, providing antioxidant support.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Tots contain slowly digestible carbs that help sustain energy and fullness.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Baking without added oil eliminates trans fats that are typical of deep‑fried snacks.

items.title: Portion control convenience
items.content: The frozen format lets you measure exact servings, helping to avoid overeating.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Even without added oil, tots are calorie‑dense due to potato and breadcrumb content.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added to the coating; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor salt intake.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may react to potato or coating ingredients.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and bake the tots for 15‑20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp. Serve as a side with burgers, grilled meats, or with dipping sauces such as ketchup, mustard, or cheese sauce. They also add crunch to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen tots in their original packaging in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F). After opening, transfer to an airtight bag to prevent freezer burn. Use within 6‑12 months for best quality.

tea-iced-brewed-green-decaffeinated-pre-.title: Tea, iced, brewed, green, decaffeinated, pre-sweetened with sugar

content.title: About
content.content: Iced brewed green tea without caffeine, pre‑sweetened with sugar, is a ready‑to‑drink beverage. It retains the light, vegetal flavor of green tea while lacking the stimulating effect of caffeine, and the added sugar makes it sweet and refreshing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is rich in polyphenols, which have antioxidant properties.
Decaffeination is usually performed by water extraction, preserving most flavor compounds.
Sweetening with sugar makes the drink popular among children and those who prefer sweet beverages.
Iced brewed tea is often sold in bottles or cans, convenient for on‑the‑go consumption.
In some countries this drink is considered an alternative to carbonated soft drinks.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Polyphenols in green tea help combat free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Low caffeine content and high water volume aid in maintaining the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: Absence of caffeine reduces the risk of nervous overstimulation, making it suitable for evening consumption.

items.title: Caffeine‑free energy boost
items.content: Sugar provides a quick source of energy, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Gentle tannins in green tea may help improve digestion.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar increases the calorie count and may contribute to tooth decay with frequent consumption.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Impact on blood glucose
items.content: The sugary beverage can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, which is important for people with diabetes to consider.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve the tea chilled, optionally over ice with a slice of lemon for extra flavor. It works well as a refreshing drink on hot days, after workouts, or as a light sweet snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the beverage refrigerated at 0 °C to 4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. Do not store at room temperature for more than 12 hours.
